action: Patients: book through other channels the hospital announces until its website and contact centre return. Health providers: confirm offline backups and a plan for running appointments without digital systems.
date_note: Emol (18 November) says the hospital's management reported the problem on Monday, which is 16 November.
exec: A hospital's online and phone booking channels were out of service, and legislators are asking whether patient records were exposed.
impact: Online booking and the contact centre were out of service, according to the hospital.
plain: The Hospital Clínico of the University of Chile in Santiago said its systems were affected, so appointments could not be booked on its website or by phone. Deputies asked whether patient records were exposed.
summary: Emol reports a cyberattack on the Hospital Clínico of the Universidad de Chile. The hospital's management said an impact on its institutional systems affected its website and its contact centre, so appointments could not be booked. Deputies filed five oversight requests asking whether patient records were compromised; the article names no actor and does not say whether data was accessed.
title: Chile's Hospital Clínico de la Universidad de Chile says systems affected, booking channels down; Emol reports a cyberattack

validation.note: Single publisher (Emol); hospital statement quoted by Emol, not read directly.

review.note: Title gave the hospital the cyberattack label, but it only said systems were affected; title now attributes it to Emol; status confirmed to developing
